key_insight: A parity-breaking cellular automaton can reproduce odd-fluid hydrodynamics, including odd viscosity, by combining chiral collisions with systematic velocity rotation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a microscopic, lattice-based route to model transport in fluids with transverse response, which is useful for understanding or designing active, magnetic, or topological flow systems.
method: Start from the FHP lattice-gas cellular automaton on a 2D triangular lattice.
Introduce chiral two-body collision rules to break parity symmetry.
Rotate particle velocities to emulate a background magnetic field and generate odd viscosity.
evidence_signal: The analytical transport coefficients were checked against Poiseuille-flow simulations of the chiral FHP automaton.
watch_item: As a discrete lattice model, the odd-viscosity behavior may depend on the chosen collision rules, rotation scheme, and coarse-graining assumptions when mapping to real fluids.
paper_title: Odd fluids from chiral cellular automata
